newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Following an outbreak of stomach infections, nearly 300,000 customers of Three Valleys Water in Watford, St Albans and parts of north west London were being told to boil their drinking water after public health officials isolated 32 cases of infections linked to contaminated water. --
OLD LADY IN NEW MARKET SHAKE-UP

The Bank of England is extending its daily money market operations to include gilt repurchase transactions, is expected to create more orderly movements on markets overnight and very short term interest rates.

Thailand's central bank today ordered that all trading in banking and finance sector shares cease as it ordered commercial banks and finance companies to raise provisions for their sub-standard assets. It also told 10 firms to increase their capital immediately. --
WEST END AND CITY OFFICE COSTS SOAR
West End offices in London are now the most expensive to run in Europe. They are the fourth costliest in the world, following Bombay, Hong Kong and central Tokyo. --
PLANS TO CUT THE COST OF CALLS TO MOBILE PHONES

An overhaul of costs of calling a mobile phone from a fixed BT telephone, is expected next month by Oftel. The proposals by the regulator could cost the Vodaphone and Cellnet networks millions of pounds a year, by cutting the charges to the mobile phone companies. -- BMC +44 171 377 1742
